tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.content:
1	# Device card — vti-02 (tetralayer graphene)
2	
3	*Session device card for vti-02 on the **VTI** cryostat. Deployed into the
4	measurement directory alongside the working notebooks. This card carries
5	**physical truth**: what is wired, the hardware, the outer safety box,
6	the provided gate operating limits, and the provided contact
7	configuration. The CNP location and (n, D) calibration are established
8	in-session (see the session brief).*
9	
10	## Identity
11	- **Device id**: `vti-02`
12	- **Material**: tetralayer graphene (`4LGr`).
13	- **Owner**: Aaron
14	- **Fridge**: VTI (variable-temperature insert). Base (sample)
15	  temperature ≈ 1.2–1.3 K.
16	- **Status**: cold, wired — hardwired breakout, no contact mux; no CNP
17	  location on record.
18	
19	## Gate stack
20	- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by a Keithley 2400**
21	  (`k_2400_tg`) — sweeps use `k_tg.volt` (5 mV step pacing; the measure
22	  notebook's setup cells bind `k_tg`).
23	- **Back gate** (`k_bg`): graphite on hBN, driven by the second
24	  **Keithley 2400** (`k_2400_bg`).
25	- **Si global back gate** (`k_si`): doped-Si gate through **SiO₂**,
26	  driven by the **SRS DC205** — bound directly to the driver's ramped
27	  parameter **`dc205.smart_voltage`** (set ramps at `ramp_rate = 0.5`
28	  V/s, get reads back `VOLT?`; data column **`dc205_smart_voltage`**).
29	  The DC205 has **no current readback** — gate-leakage monitoring lives
30	  on the Keithley `curr` channels (TG/BG) only. `ramp_voltage` steps
31	  span/50: a full ±50 V traverse moves in ~1 V steps, paced by
32	  `ramp_rate`. The graphite back gate screens Si from the channel — Si
33	  couples only to the contacts (contact-doping gate). Operating limit
34	  provided (below).
35	- **Gate-stack geometry** (fabrication facts; **geometry prior only** —
36	  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via
37	  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`):
38	  ```python
39	  from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages
40	  c_tg = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)])           # 9.5 nm hBN
41	  c_bg = stack_capacitance([(11, 3), (0, 3.9)])   # 11 nm hBN, no SiO2 term
42	  ```
43	  Treat anything derived from these (lever arms, n/D scales, CNP-line
44	  slope) as uncalibrated until the session's own gate map confirms it.
45	
46	## Gate operating limits — gate B contract
47	
48	Gate operating limits for the session:
49	
50	| Parameter | Operating limit | Notes |
51	|---|---|---|
52	| `k_tg.volt` | **[−0.3, +1.0] V** | provided; geometry ceiling is the hard fence behind it |
53	| `k_bg.volt` | **[−1.3, +2.0] V** | provided |
54	| `dc205.smart_voltage` / `dc205.voltage` (Si) | **[−25, +25] V** | provided; DC205 must be on its ±100 V range (RNGE 2) |
55	| **B field (session cap)** | **\|B\| ≤ 10.0 T** | committed on the `magnet.field` validator (SAFETIES); driver `max_field_T = 14.0` T is the hard backstop |
56	| **T setpoint (session cap)** | **`set_both` target ≤ 100 K** | provided; committed as a SAFETIES setpoint typo-guard cap. `ratio = 0.95` per the rig card — deviations consent-gated |
57	
58	## Measurement setup (rig instruments wired this cooldown)
59	- **Gates**: top via **k_2400_tg** (GPIB0::1), back via **k_2400_bg**
60	  (GPIB0::24), hardwired to their sources.
61	- **Si gate**: **DC205** (`dc205.smart_voltage`, ASRL7, ±100 V
62	  range), hardwired to its source.
63	- **AC excitation / lock-ins**: SR830 family (`sr0` GPIB0::22, `sr1` GPIB0::14, `sr2` GPIB0::19, `sr3` GPIB0::18).
64	  Current-bias drive through a **100 MOhm** bias resistor, lock-in
65	  frequency **13.777 Hz**.
66	- **Current channel**: **`sr0`** = drain current, **`sr0_gain = −1E6`**
67	  (preamp gain). Per-channel sensitivities are recorded per run in
68	  `measurement_config`.
69	- **Drive / bias channel**: **`sr1`** — the lock-in whose
70	  oscillator provides the current-bias drive; `I_bias` = its live amplitude
71	  / the bias resistor. `hera-watch` reads the drive here.
72	- **Contacts — hardwired, no mux this cooldown**: device pads bond to
73	  two Fischer cables and land on the breakout; instrument leads connect
74	  directly there. Contact roles are **fixed** — rerouting a pair is
75	  operator work at the breakout, not software.
76	  - **Contact map**:
77	
78	    Bonded pads (label = position, T = top arc L→R, B = left side then
79	    bottom L→R). Only the provided configuration below is wired to
80	    instruments this cooldown:

# Device card — vti-02 (tetralayer graphene)

*Session device card for vti-02 on the **VTI** cryostat. Deployed into the
measurement directory alongside the working notebooks. This card carries
**physical truth**: what is wired, the hardware, the outer safety box,
the provided gate operating limits, and the provided contact
configuration. The CNP location and (n, D) calibration are established
in-session (see the session brief).*

## Identity
- **Device id**: `vti-02`
- **Material**: tetralayer graphene (`4LGr`).
- **Owner**: Aaron
- **Fridge**: VTI (variable-temperature insert). Base (sample)
  temperature ≈ 1.2–1.3 K.
- **Status**: cold, wired — hardwired breakout, no contact mux; no CNP
  location on record.

## Gate stack
- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by a Keithley 2400**
  (`k_2400_tg`) — sweeps use `k_tg.volt` (5 mV step pacing; the measure
  notebook's setup cells bind `k_tg`).
- **Back gate** (`k_bg`): graphite on hBN, driven by the second
  **Keithley 2400** (`k_2400_bg`).
- **Si global back gate** (`k_si`): doped-Si gate through **SiO₂**,
  driven by the **SRS DC205** — bound directly to the driver's ramped
  parameter **`dc205.smart_voltage`** (set ramps at `ramp_rate = 0.5`
  V/s, get reads back `VOLT?`; data column **`dc205_smart_voltage`**).
  The DC205 has **no current readback** — gate-leakage monitoring lives
  on the Keithley `curr` channels (TG/BG) only. `ramp_voltage` steps
  span/50: a full ±50 V traverse moves in ~1 V steps, paced by
  `ramp_rate`. The graphite back gate screens Si from the channel — Si
  couples only to the contacts (contact-doping gate). Operating limit
  provided (below).
- **Gate-stack geometry** (fabrication facts; **geometry prior only** —
  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via
  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`):
  ```python
  from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages
  c_tg = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)])           # 9.5 nm hBN
  c_bg = stack_capacitance([(11, 3), (0, 3.9)])   # 11 nm hBN, no SiO2 term
  ```
  Treat anything derived from these (lever arms, n/D scales, CNP-line
  slope) as uncalibrated until the session's own gate map confirms it.

## Gate operating limits — gate B contract

Gate operating limits for the session:

| Parameter | Operating limit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `k_tg.volt` | **[−0.3, +1.0] V** | provided; geometry ceiling is the hard fence behind it |
| `k_bg.volt` | **[−1.3, +2.0] V** | provided |
| `dc205.smart_voltage` / `dc205.voltage` (Si) | **[−25, +25] V** | provided; DC205 must be on its ±100 V range (RNGE 2) |
| **B field (session cap)** | **\|B\| ≤ 10.0 T** | committed on the `magnet.field` validator (SAFETIES); driver `max_field_T = 14.0` T is the hard backstop |
| **T setpoint (session cap)** | **`set_both` target ≤ 100 K** | provided; committed as a SAFETIES setpoint typo-guard cap. `ratio = 0.95` per the rig card — deviations consent-gated |

## Measurement setup (rig instruments wired this cooldown)
- **Gates**: top via **k_2400_tg** (GPIB0::1), back via **k_2400_bg**
  (GPIB0::24), hardwired to their sources.
- **Si gate**: **DC205** (`dc205.smart_voltage`, ASRL7, ±100 V
  range), hardwired to its source.
- **AC excitation / lock-ins**: SR830 family (`sr0` GPIB0::22, `sr1` GPIB0::14, `sr2` GPIB0::19, `sr3` GPIB0::18).
  Current-bias drive through a **100 MOhm** bias resistor, lock-in
  frequency **13.777 Hz**.
- **Current channel**: **`sr0`** = drain current, **`sr0_gain = −1E6`**
  (preamp gain). Per-channel sensitivities are recorded per run in
  `measurement_config`.
- **Drive / bias channel**: **`sr1`** — the lock-in whose
  oscillator provides the current-bias drive; `I_bias` = its live amplitude
  / the bias resistor. `hera-watch` reads the drive here.
- **Contacts — hardwired, no mux this cooldown**: device pads bond to
  two Fischer cables and land on the breakout; instrument leads connect
  directly there. Contact roles are **fixed** — rerouting a pair is
  operator work at the breakout, not software.
  - **Contact map**:

    Bonded pads (label = position, T = top arc L→R, B = left side then
    bottom L→R). Only the provided configuration below is wired to
    instruments this cooldown:

    | Label | Pad | | Label | Pad |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    |  -  | -  | | T_0 | 29 |
    | B_1 | 12 | | T_1 | 41 |
    | B_2 | 04 | | T_2 | 01 |
    | B_3 | 27 | | T_3 | 42 |
    |  -  | -  | | T_4 | 43 |

    Alive: T_0, B_1, B_2, B_3. Dead: T_1, T_2, T_3, T_4. Liveness on the provided configuration is
    re-confirmed at Gate C.
- **Provided contact configuration** (hardwired):

  | role | label |
  |---|---|
  | source        | T_0 |
  | drain (`sr0`) | B_3 |
  | `sr1` (Rxx)   | B_1 - B_2 |
  | `sr2` (Rxx)   | n.c. |
  | `sr3` (Rxx)   | n.c. |

## Notes

Lock-in gains: `sr1` 1 (unity); `sr2`, `sr3` n.c.

23	  (raw TCP `192.168.0.10:10001`). Out-of-plane field, Tesla, via the
24	  `field` qcodes Parameter.
25	- **Coil constant**: `T_per_A = 1/7.3` ≈ 0.137 T/A.
26	- **Ramp rate**: fixed 1 A/min ≈ **0.137 T/min**, hard-coded in the
27	  driver and sent with every setpoint. An 8 T traverse is a ~58 min
28	  floor.
29	- **Set semantics**: `magnet.field(target)` **blocks** until the field
30	  is reached (polls the ramping flag, then a `settle_s` dwell — default
31	  3 s, tunable). A cell that ramps is busy the whole ramp.
32	- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: interrupting the notebook cell does **not**
33	  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
34	  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `field()` again
35	  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
36	  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.
37	- **Magnet limit**: **14.0 T** (Zack ruling 2026-06-12), enforced by
38	  the driver (`max_field_T = 14.0`; ramping above it raises). The
39	  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
40	  `magnet.field.vals`) is what measurements obey.
41	- **High field + elevated T interact through the probe's coupling to
42	  the bath**; not expected to bite below ~100 K (heuristic — Aaron,
43	  2026-08-02, bath-vs-probe-T response unmeasured).
44	- **Read-truth**: `field()`'s get returns the **measured** output
45	  current × `T_per_A` (`GET:I:?`, 2-stage moving-average readback,
46	  ~41 ms lag ≈ 0.1 mT at our slew). The set-point is not readable as
47	  field; never infer field from the last set call.
48	- **Persistent switch / output**: heater `heater_on()` / `heater_off()`
49	  (each blocks 10 s, **no field-matching check** — operator-only);
50	  state reads `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()`.
51	- **Never re-traverse**: the fixed slow ramp makes field the expensive
52	  axis. Plan sweeps to start where the magnet sits and end where the
53	  next measurement needs it; alternate fan directions across
54	  iterations rather than returning to a preferred start field.
55	
56	## Thermometry & heaters
57	
58	- **Controller**: Lakeshore 335 (`drivers.Lakeshore_335`).
59	  Input A = sample-mount Cernox (`sample_temperature`, `KRDG? A`);
60	  input B = vaporizer Cernox (`vaporizer_temperature`, `KRDG? B`).
61	- **Readout is file-based, never GPIB**: the lakeshore worker (VTI
62	  Monitor launcher) owns LS335 polling and writes InfluxDB (`vti`) plus
63	  `C:\Users\DGG\temperature_logs\VTI_{sample,vaporizer}.txt`. Logfile
64	  cadence **5 s** (InfluxDB 30 s; worker `READ_INTERVAL`, 2026-07-16).
65	  Freshness guards must allow **≥ 2–3 write periods** — a threshold
66	  equal to the cadence false-fires at end-of-period (burned: ladder v2,
67	  2026-07-15). The kernel
68	  reads `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer` via
69	  `temperature_from_logfiles(VTI.temp_logfile_candidates[...])`,
70	  `fp()`-able as recorded channels; the `heater` instance is control-only
71	  (setpoints / ranges / power). A frozen logfile (dead worker) reads a
72	  plausible value that `assert T < base` cannot catch — at bring-up
73	  confirm the logfile mtime is advancing.
74	- **Sensors**: 2× CX-1030-CU-HT-0.3M (serials X225149, X225150),
75	  NIST-traceable ITS-90, 0.3–420 K. Calibration packages in-repo at
76	  `hera/vti/cernox-cal/` (INDEX.md has the error budget). Curve
77	  assignments (read from NVRAM 2026-06-12): **input A = curve 23,
78	  serial X225149**; input B = curve 21, whose header *also* reads
79	  X225149 — likely X225150's data loaded under an unedited name, or a
80	  duplicate load of A's curve. Impact is bounded by the inter-sensor
81	  cal delta and B is control-only, but the anomaly is unresolved
82	  (Bingcheng).
83	- **Accuracy**: ±6–9 mK at 10–20 K, zero-field. Field-induced error:
84	  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
85	  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
86	  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
87	- **Control topology**: both LS335 loops are closed-loop (loop 1
88	  sample-mount heater ↔ input A; loop 2 vaporizer ↔ input B). The
89	  sanctioned elevated-T method is **`heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`**,
90	  authorized **≤ 100 K** (Aaron, 2026-07-18, via Zack). The **needle
91	  valve remains operator-only, hands at the rig**.
92	- **Sample-loop PID is untuned** (confirmed live 2026-07-15): upward
93	  setpoint steps overshoot **~+1.4 K**, and recovery is bath-limited —
94	  the sample cools only toward the vaporizer floor at `ratio·T`, so
95	  the overshoot penalty scales with (1 − ratio). At ratio 0.99:
96	  ~0.015 K/min recovery; tolerance-settling never passed below ~20 K.
97	  Accept elevated-T points on *stability*, not proximity (hover
98	  acceptance — temperature-dependence VTI variant). Tuning backlogged
99	  (eng-backlog, Bingcheng).
100	- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
101	  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
102	  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.
103	
104	
105	## Silent preconditions
106	
107	Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
108	bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
109	each. (LS335 control instance is named `heater`; temperature is read from
110	the worker logfiles via `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer`.)
111	
112	| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
113	|---|---|---|---|
114	| Sample temperature | `T_sample()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
115	| Magnet field | `magnet.field()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
116	| Vaporizer state | `T_vaporizer()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
117	| PS heater / output | `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()` | heater on, output enabled (`field()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |
118	
119	## Sweep stack & data layout
120	
121	The `sweep` package (measureme submodule) is the single source of truth for the
122	station/sweep call surface, the on-disk run format, and the metadata schema:
123	`docs/api/measureme.md`. Stations are built with `sweep.AsyncStation`. Rig
124	specifics:
125	
126	- **Measurement dir**: each sweep writes `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/`,
127	  the measurement dir being `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`.
128	- **`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement** — for rastered /
129	  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the TSV before
130	  any visual read.
131	- **Mixed metadata on disk**: this rig's corpus spans both schema versions
132	  (older singular keys; current plural + `version`/`instruments`). Load through
133	  `hera.analysis` / `sweep.sweep_load`, never hand-rolled.
134	
135	## Timing rules of thumb
136	
137	Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
138	current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
139	calibrating run.
140	
141	- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
142	  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
143	  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
144	  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
145	  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
146	  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
147	- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
148	  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
149	  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
150	  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
151	  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
152	- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
153	  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
154	- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
155	  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
156	  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
157	  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
158	- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
159	  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
160	  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
161	  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
162	- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
163	  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
164	  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
165	  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
166	  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
167	  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.
168	
169	## Standard equipment
170	
171	Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
172	hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict.
173	
174	- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
175	  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
176	  **Settling**: `time_constant` + `filter_slope` are operator-set on the
177	  front panel and **not set by the kit** — read them (`srN.time_constant()`,
178	  `srN.filter_slope()`) at bring-up and record them, so the swept-point dwell
179	  (`≳ k·τ`; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct) can be priced against a
180	  known τ and bent knowingly, not guessed (STYLE rule 12 settling floor). The
181	  run-metadata `instruments` snapshot currently stores these as `None` —
182	  until that's fixed, the bring-up record is the only place τ lives on disk.
183	- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
184	  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
185	  `measurement_config`.
186	- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud, **ASRL7**,
187	  s/n 20500514) — use `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp,
188	  deterministic dV/dt); the
189	  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
190	  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
191	  The Keithley `volt.step`, the DC205 `ramp_rate`, and `inter_delay` are
192	  operator-owned — the agent never changes them.
193	- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
194	  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
195	  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
196	  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
197	  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
198	  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), **ASRL4**.
199	  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
200	  (read `mux.settle_s`).
201	  Per-cooldown bless status (validated address, any `settle_s` override)
202	  lives in the device card; `ContactMux` is live only when the device
203	  card says so. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps are wiring → (per-device).
204	- **Terranova 906A gauge**: serial, **ASRL8** — held by the
205	  influx-logger kernel.
206	- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
207	  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
208	- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
209	  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.
210	
211	## Known quirks
212	
213	- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
214	  to address unicode issues.
215	
216	## What this card does not carry
217	
218	- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
219	  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
220	- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
221	- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
222	  device card + SAFETIES cell.
223	- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
224	  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
225	  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.
226

  X225149 — likely X225150's data loaded under an unedited name, or a
  duplicate load of A's curve. Impact is bounded by the inter-sensor
  cal delta and B is control-only, but the anomaly is unresolved
  (Bingcheng).
- **Accuracy**: ±6–9 mK at 10–20 K, zero-field. Field-induced error:
  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
- **Control topology**: both LS335 loops are closed-loop (loop 1
  sample-mount heater ↔ input A; loop 2 vaporizer ↔ input B). The
  sanctioned elevated-T method is **`heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`**,
  authorized **≤ 100 K** (Aaron, 2026-07-18, via Zack). The **needle
  valve remains operator-only, hands at the rig**.
- **Sample-loop PID is untuned** (confirmed live 2026-07-15): upward
  setpoint steps overshoot **~+1.4 K**, and recovery is bath-limited —
  the sample cools only toward the vaporizer floor at `ratio·T`, so
  the overshoot penalty scales with (1 − ratio). At ratio 0.99:
  ~0.015 K/min recovery; tolerance-settling never passed below ~20 K.
  Accept elevated-T points on *stability*, not proximity (hover
  acceptance — temperature-dependence VTI variant). Tuning backlogged
  (eng-backlog, Bingcheng).
- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.


## Silent preconditions

Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
each. (LS335 control instance is named `heater`; temperature is read from
the worker logfiles via `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer`.)

| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sample temperature | `T_sample()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
| Magnet field | `magnet.field()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
| Vaporizer state | `T_vaporizer()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
| PS heater / output | `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()` | heater on, output enabled (`field()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |

## Sweep stack & data layout

The `sweep` package (measureme submodule) is the single source of truth for the
station/sweep call surface, the on-disk run format, and the metadata schema:
`docs/api/measureme.md`. Stations are built with `sweep.AsyncStation`. Rig
specifics:

- **Measurement dir**: each sweep writes `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/`,
  the measurement dir being `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`.
- **`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement** — for rastered /
  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the TSV before
  any visual read.
- **Mixed metadata on disk**: this rig's corpus spans both schema versions
  (older singular keys; current plural + `version`/`instruments`). Load through
  `hera.analysis` / `sweep.sweep_load`, never hand-rolled.

## Timing rules of thumb

Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
calibrating run.

- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.

## Standard equipment

Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict.

- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
  **Settling**: `time_constant` + `filter_slope` are operator-set on the
  front panel and **not set by the kit** — read them (`srN.time_constant()`,
  `srN.filter_slope()`) at bring-up and record them, so the swept-point dwell
  (`≳ k·τ`; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct) can be priced against a
  known τ and bent knowingly, not guessed (STYLE rule 12 settling floor). The
  run-metadata `instruments` snapshot currently stores these as `None` —
  until that's fixed, the bring-up record is the only place τ lives on disk.
- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
  `measurement_config`.
- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud, **ASRL7**,
  s/n 20500514) — use `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp,
  deterministic dV/dt); the
  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
  The Keithley `volt.step`, the DC205 `ramp_rate`, and `inter_delay` are
  operator-owned — the agent never changes them.
- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), **ASRL4**.
  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
  (read `mux.settle_s`).
  Per-cooldown bless status (validated address, any `settle_s` override)
  lives in the device card; `ContactMux` is live only when the device
  card says so. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps are wiring → (per-device).
- **Terranova 906A gauge**: serial, **ASRL8** — held by the
  influx-logger kernel.
- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.

## Known quirks

- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
  to address unicode issues.

## What this card does not carry

- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
  device card + SAFETIES cell.
- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.

}=== ana_cal_md ===
## Run 5 — 0 T gatemap (`gatemap`) → `cnp-and-dline-calibration`

Raw map (log R, TG fast [−0.3, +1.0] × BG slow [−1.3, +1.2], 20 × 40 mV, sr1 100 µV; run 4 was the same map aborted at 3 min when the ridge railed at 2 kΩ). **Read:** one dominant CNP ridge (A) running from (V_tg, V_bg) ≈ (+1.0, −1.3) to (−0.3, +0.45), plus a fainter **parallel** ridge (B) ≈ 0.19 V lower in V_tg — the second peak of runs 0–3. Ridge A's resistance is 240 Ω near D ≈ 0 and grows to ~2.4 kΩ at raw D ≈ +0.25 V/nm (saturating beyond), i.e. a D-tunable gap; **not a stacking read** (investigation Step 1 addendum: three candidate parents). Fits (ridge position = V_tg vs V_bg rows, so −slope = c_bg/c_tg): ridge A in the operating window |V_bg| < 0.5: slope −0.773 (rms 19 mV); high-D rows: −0.763 (rms 6 mV); ridge B: −0.69 (8 rows, rms 13 mV). **Calibration:** ratio c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data-calibrated; prior 0.864, −11 % — plausible hBN-thickness error, not a transposition); c_tg anchored at the 9.5 nm prior (absolute scale = geometry prior, pending a lever-arm check); n_offset = −0.089×10¹²; **D_offset from the R_CNP(D) symmetry** (vertex of the ridge-A resistance minimum, ≈ +0.012 raw) — the one feature that physically locates D = 0. Region B is electron-doped by 0.43×10¹² relative to A: a series-mosaic confound (same template expected, 13 % higher n at the fan density — extra tones at ×1.13). Realized D = 0 window inside the validators: **n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹²** (TG-limited on both ends). Channel arithmetic: R = (sr1_X/1)/(sr0_X/−1e6).
=== md_spot_e ===
## HERA — Step 3: SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = +3.2×10¹² at D = 0, B 0 → 10 T

Calibration from run 5 (ana): c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data), c_tg = 2.796 mF/m² (9.5 nm prior), n_offset −0.089×10¹², D_offset −0.013 V/nm (R_CNP(D) symmetry). The D = 0 line inside the validators spans n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹², so the electron side is the high-|n| side: spot at **n = +3.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (+0.984, +1.166) V, 16 mV under the TG limit. **Feasibility (Step 2, model table):** F_L = 33.1 T; ABAB pair ≈ 7.5 / 25.6 T (m* 0.028 / 0.061 mₑ), ABCA singleton 33.1 T (m* 0.074); the heavy-ABAB-vs-ABCA split is 7.5 T. Grid: uniform in B (blocking magnet) — 50 mT from 0 to 1 T (MR background only; LK at T_e ≈ 8 K kills m* = 0.06 below ~1.5 T), **10 mT from 1 to 10 T**; 921 points. Dwell: `delay = 0` — each `magnet.field` set blocks through the ramp plus the driver's 3 s settle = 10 τ at τ = 0.3 s / 24 dB, i.e. the lock-in is at the settling floor at every point. Sensitivity fixed at 50 µV (5 kΩ FS): R(B = 0) ≈ 70 Ω is 1.4 % of range, but there is no SdH below ~1.5 T and the MR + SdH maxima at high B need the headroom; the FFT window starts above onset. **Price:** 10 T bare traverse 73 min + 921 × ~3.8 s per-point overhead (settle 3 s + reads) ≈ 58 min → **≈ 2 h 15 m**, ending at **10 T with the gates at the spot** — the hole-side spot check (n = −1.2×10¹²) then rides the magnet down 10 → 0.3 T, never re-traversing. Checkpoints: first 20 points (signal, sensitivity, leakage, field readback tracking setpoints); at ~3 T and ~6 T a partial FFT on the landed record (onset, tone count) — abort if the channel rails or no oscillation content has appeared by 6 T with R flat (then the fan is pointless at this T_e and the read is resolution-limited).
=== md_spot_h ===
## HERA — Step 3b: SdH spot check, hole side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = −1.2×10¹² at D = 0, riding the magnet 10 → 0.3 T

Run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹²) ends at 10 T with the gates at the spot. The investigation takes both signs (no side prior); the hole side of the D = 0 line reaches only n = −1.27×10¹² (TG −0.3 V limit), so the spot sits at **n = −1.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (−0.280, −0.463) V. Feasibility (model): F_L = 12.4 T; ABAB pair ≈ 5.3 / 7.1 T (the near-CNP semimetal regime, tones close and balanced — the recipe's stated low-|n| exception), ABCA 12.4 T with m* ≈ 1 mₑ — LK-dead at this rig's T_e ≈ 8 K. **Coverage trade, stated:** this is a cheap preview, not a decisive read — it costs ~35 min over the bare 10 → 0 T ramp the session needs anyway, and a null here is resolvability-limited, not evidence. Grid: 20 mT uniform in B descending, 486 pts, delay 0 (3 s driver settle = 10 τ). Sensitivity 50 µV (5 kΩ FS; R(B = 0) ≈ 250–300 Ω this close to the CNP, MR headroom). Price: 9.7 T traverse 71 min + 486 × ~3.8 s ≈ 31 min → **≈ 1 h 45 m**, ending at 0.3 T. Checkpoints: first 20 points (rail? the CNP side at 10 T could be large), then the ana read at the end together with run 6.

# === SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`): n = +3.2e12 at D = 0 (region-A calibration), B 0 -> 10 T ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
n_spot, D_spot = 3.2, 0.0                       # 1e12 cm^-2, V/nm
Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot = calc_gate_voltages(n_spot, D_spot, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert TG_MIN <= Vtg_spot <= TG_MAX and BG_MIN <= Vbg_spot <= BG_MAX, (Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot)
print(f"spot: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm -> (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}) V; "
      f"roundtrip n,D = {calc_nD(Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])}")

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: sweep starts at 0), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# --- field grid: uniform in B (blocking rate-limited magnet). 50 mT to 1 T (background only), 10 mT 1 -> 10 T:
B_vec = np.unique(np.round(np.hstack((np.arange(0.0, 1.0, 0.05), np.arange(1.0, 10.0001, 0.01))), 4))
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP
I_TRIP = 1e-9
# Fixed sensitivity: 50 uV = 5 kOhm full scale at 10 nA (R(B=0) ~ 70 Ohm = 1.4 % FS; MR + SdH maxima at high B size the headroom).
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
print(f"B grid: {len(B_vec)} pts, {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T; sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s (settle_s {magnet.settle_s} s = dwell)")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = f"sdh-spot-check electron: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm (run-5 cal), (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}), B 0 -> 10 T, 10 mT above 1 T, sr1 50 uV"
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('sdh-spot-check')
s.add_comment(f'electron side: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12 cm^-2, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm; (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}); '
              f'B 0 -> 10 T uniform-B (50 mT to 1 T, 10 mT above); cal run 5: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f}')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_spot); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_spot)
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B, T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(magnet.field, sr1.X); s.plot(magnet.field, sr0.X); s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

s.sweep(magnet.field, B_vec, delay=0)
# gates stay at the spot; field stays at 10 T (the hole-side spot check rides it down) — no park here.
print(f"done: B = {magnet.field():+.3f} T, (Vtg, Vbg) = ({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f})")

"""cnp-and-dline-calibration on gatemap run 5: per-row ridge extraction (two ridges), ratio fit on the
operating window near D = 0, offsets, closure check, realized D = 0 n-window; writes cal params to JSON."""
import sys, json, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from hera.analysis import fan_grids, resistance_grids
from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages

rid = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 5
g = fan_grids(f"data/{rid}"); rg = resistance_grids(g)
R = np.abs(rg.R["sr1"]); Vbg = g.slow
fs = g.meta["fast_setpoints"]; Vtg = np.asarray(fs[0] if isinstance(fs[0], list) else fs)
c_tg0 = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)]); c_bg0 = stack_capacitance([(11, 3)])
print(f"run {rid}: {g.nrows} rows x {g.nfast}; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; prior c_bg/c_tg = {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}")

# ridge extraction: per row, up to two peaks; track continuity from the high-|D| end where ridge A is unambiguous
pts = []   # (Vbg, Vtg, R, ridge)
for i in range(g.nrows):
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0)
    pk, _ = find_peaks(r, prominence=0.05 * (r.max() - r.min()) + 5)
    pk = [p for p in pk if 1 < p < g.nfast - 2]
    for p in sorted(pk, key=lambda p: -r[p])[:2]:
        pts.append((Vbg[i], Vtg[p], r[p]))
pts = np.array(pts)
# assign to ridges by distance to the high-D fit of ridge A (rows Vbg < -0.6), then refit each
selA = pts[:, 0] < -0.6
cfA0 = np.polyfit(pts[selA, 0], pts[selA, 1], 1)
dist = pts[:, 1] - np.polyval(cfA0, pts[:, 0])
ridgeA = pts[np.abs(dist) < 0.08]; ridgeB = pts[(dist < -0.08) & (dist > -0.45)]

def fit(p, lo, hi, label):
    m = (p[:, 0] >= lo) & (p[:, 0] <= hi)
    x, y = p[m, 0], p[m, 1]
    if len(x) < 4: print(f"{label}: {len(x)} rows, skip"); return None
    keep = np.ones(len(x), bool)
    for _ in range(3):
        cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = y - np.polyval(cf, x)
        keep = np.abs(res) < 2.5 * max(np.std(res[keep]), 0.01)
    cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = (y - np.polyval(cf, x))[keep]
    print(f"{label}: {keep.sum()}/{len(x)} rows, Vbg [{lo:+.2f},{hi:+.2f}]: Vtg = {cf[0]:+.4f} Vbg {cf[1]:+.4f}; "
          f"c_bg/c_tg = {-cf[0]:.3f}; rms {np.std(res)*1e3:.1f} mV")
    return cf

print("--- ridge A (main) ---")
cfA_all = fit(ridgeA, -2, 2, "A all rows")
cfA_hiD = fit(ridgeA, -2, -0.6, "A high-D rows")
cfA_op = fit(ridgeA, -0.5, 0.5, "A operating window |Vbg|<0.5")
print("--- ridge B (parallel, lower Vtg) ---")
cfB_all = fit(ridgeB, -2, 2, "B all rows")
cfB_op = fit(ridgeB, -0.5, 0.5, "B operating window")

# calibration: anchor c_tg at the prior (single hBN dielectric, better constrained), set c_bg from the operating-window ratio
cf = cfA_op if cfA_op is not None else cfA_all
ratio = -cf[0]; c_tg = c_tg0; c_bg = ratio * c_tg
n0, _ = calc_nD(cf[1], 0.0, c_tg, c_bg); n_offset = -n0
nA_ridge = calc_nD(np.polyval(cf, ridgeA[:, 0]), ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0]
print(f"\nCALIBRATION (ridge A, operating window): ratio {ratio:.3f} (prior {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}, {100*(ratio/(c_bg0/c_tg0)-1):+.0f}%), "
      f"c_tg {c_tg:.3e} F/m2 (prior anchor), c_bg {c_bg:.3e}; n_offset {n_offset:+.4f}e12; closure max|n| on fitted line {np.abs(nA_ridge).max():.3f}e12")
nB = calc_nD(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0] if len(ridgeB) else np.array([np.nan])
print(f"ridge B density offset relative to A: n_B = {np.nanmedian(nB):+.3f}e12 (std {np.nanstd(nB):.3f}), i.e. region B is {'hole' if np.nanmedian(nB)>0 else 'electron'}-doped vs A by {abs(np.nanmedian(nB)):.2f}e12")
# D = 0 line of region A: V_tg = (c_bg/c_tg) V_bg + V_tg0 where n=0 at ... use calc_gate_voltages
ns = np.linspace(-1.5, 4.5, 601); Vt, Vb = calc_gate_voltages(ns, np.zeros_like(ns), c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
ok = (Vt >= -0.3) & (Vt <= 1.0) & (Vb >= -1.3) & (Vb <= 2.0)
print(f"D = 0 line (region A) realized n-window inside validators: {ns[ok].min():+.2f} .. {ns[ok].max():+.2f} e12; "
      f"CNP at (Vtg, Vbg) = ({calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[0]:+.3f}, {calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[1]:+.3f})")
# D range along ridge A
DA = calc_nD(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[1]
print(f"ridge A spans D = {DA.min():+.3f} .. {DA.max():+.3f} V/nm; peak R vs D: " +
      ", ".join(f"{d:+.2f}:{r:.0f}" for d, r in sorted(zip(np.round(DA, 2), ridgeA[:, 2]))[::6]))
json.dump({"run": rid, "ratio": ratio, "c_tg": c_tg, "c_bg": c_bg, "n_offset": n_offset, "D_offset": 0.0,
           "slope": cf[0], "intercept": cf[1], "window": "A |Vbg|<0.5", "nB_offset": float(np.nanmedian(nB))},
          open("hera_scratch/cal_run5.json", "w"), indent=1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.5))
m = ax[0].pcolormesh(Vtg, Vbg, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m, ax=ax[0], label="log10 |Rxx| (Ohm)")
ax[0].plot(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], "c.", ms=3, label="ridge A pts"); ax[0].plot(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], "g.", ms=3, label="ridge B pts")
xx = np.array([Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()])
ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cf, xx), xx, "w--", lw=1, label=f"A fit (op. window): slope {cf[0]:+.3f}")
if cfB_all is not None: ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cfB_all, xx), xx, "g--", lw=1, label=f"B fit: slope {cfB_all[0]:+.3f}")
ax[0].plot(Vt[ok], Vb[ok], "y:", lw=1.5, label="D = 0 (calibrated)")
ax[0].set_xlim(Vtg.min(), Vtg.max()); ax[0].set_ylim(Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()); ax[0].set_xlabel("V_tg (V)"); ax[0].set_ylabel("V_bg (V)")
ax[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right"); ax[0].set_title(f"run {rid} gatemap — ridges + calibration")
# (n, D) projection
N, D = calc_nD(Vtg[None, :], Vbg[:, None], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
m2 = ax[1].pcolormesh(N, D, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m2, ax=ax[1], label="log10 |Rxx|")
ax[1].axhline(0, color="y", ls=":", lw=1); ax[1].set_xlabel("n (1e12 cm^-2)"); ax[1].set_ylabel("D (V/nm)"); ax[1].set_title("(n, D) projection, region-A calibration")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"hera_scratch/cnp_cal_run{rid}.png", dpi=110); print("saved hera_scratch/cnp_cal_run5.png")

1	# `hera.analysis` API Reference
2	
3	Analysis primitives for `sweep` runs: open + summarize a run, resolve lock-in
4	channels and gains, re-form 2D fans into grids, compute gain-applied
5	resistances, and the Shubnikov–de Haas / gate-calibration math.
6	
7	Source: `src/hera/analysis.py`. Depends only on `numpy` + `scipy`.
8	
9	A *run* is a directory written by `sweep`: `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless, one row
10	per setpoint) + `metadata.json` (column names, sweep config, comments).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## Loading runs
15	
16	### `open_run(path)` → `Run`
17	Open a run directory (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Loads `metadata.json` and
18	`data.tsv(.gz)` into an `(rows, ncols)` float array; raises if the directory,
19	`metadata.json`, the `columns` entry, or the TSV is missing, or if the column
20	count disagrees with `metadata['columns']`.
21	
22	### `Run` (dataclass)
23	`Run(path, meta, cols, data)`.
24	
25	| member | description |
26	|---|---|
27	| `col(name)` | column `name` as a 1-D array; raises `KeyError` if absent, `ValueError` if the name is duplicated (use `col_at`) |
28	| `col_at(idx)` | column by index |
29	| `col_indices(name)` | all indices with column name `name` |
30	| `metadata` | alias for `meta` (the parsed `metadata.json` dict) |
31	| `recipe` | first metadata comment (conventional recipe slug), or `None` |
32	| `tags` | comments after the first |
33	| `swept_axis` | `metadata['param']` (1D sweeps) |
34	| `setpoints` | `metadata['setpoints']` as a list, or `None` |
35	| `interrupted` | `metadata['interrupted']` |
36	| `kind` | `metadata['type']` (`'0D'`/`'1D'`/`'2D'`) |
37	| `rows` | row count |
38	
39	Duplicate column names occur (planned setpoint + readback share a name; some
40	older data has two `T` columns). `col(name)` raises on duplicates — resolve
41	with `col_indices` + `col_at`.
42	
43	### `summarize_run(run)` → `str`
44	Multi-line human summary: recipe, type, sweep range + monotonicity, row
45	completeness vs planned setpoints, and mean/range T if a `T` column is present.
46	Lines with no data are omitted.
47	
48	---
49	
50	## Lock-in channel / gain model
51	
52	Shared with `hera.watch`. The physical value of a lock-in `*_X` column is
53	`X / gain`, with the gain read from `measurement_config` — never hardcode it.
54	
55	### `resolve_channels(meta, include=None)` → `list[Channel]`
56	Resolve every `_X` (in-phase) column into a `Channel`. Gains and role labels
57	come from `meta['measurement_config']`, matched `srN_X` ↔ `srN_gain` by the
58	channel's trailing integer (so both `sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain` and `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`
59	resolve); missing/zero gain defaults to `1.0`. `include` restricts to given
60	channel ids or column names. A channel `is_current` (reported as amps, not
61	converted to resistance) when its gain is negative, `|gain| ≥ 1e4`, or its
62	label mentions "current".
63	
64	### `Channel` (dataclass)
65	`col` (e.g. `'sr0_X'`), `idx` (column index), `cid` (id without `_X`), `n`
66	(trailing-integer index), `gain`, `label` (mc role string), `is_current`.
67	
68	### `current_channel(channels)` → `Channel | None`
69	The single transimpedance current channel, or `None` if not exactly one. This
70	is the denominator of four-probe resistance R = V / I.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Fan re-forming and resistances
75	
76	### `fan_grids(run, columns=None)` → `FanGrids`
77	Re-form a 2D fan (a flat-row `megasweep`/`multimegasweep`) into per-column
78	grids, keeping only complete slow rows. `run` is a directory, path, or loaded
79	`Run`. `nfast` (points per slow row) comes from `metadata['fast_setpoints']`
80	— never hardcoded; trailing partial rows of an in-progress sweep are dropped
81	(`nrows = total // nfast`). `columns` restricts which columns are retained.
82	
83	### `FanGrids` (dataclass)
84	`nrows`, `nfast`, `cols`, `data` (truncated to whole rows), `meta`,
85	`slow_param`.
86	- `grid(name)` → `(nrows, nfast)` array (duplicate names resolve to the first
87	  occurrence, i.e. the planned setpoint).
88	- `slow` → slow-axis value per row, `(nrows,)`.
89	- `metadata` → alias for `meta`.
90	
91	### `resistance_grids(fan, channels=None)` → `ResistanceGrids`
92	Per-channel four-probe resistance grids `R = (V / gain_V) / I` from a
93	`FanGrids`, where `I` is the **measured** drain current
94	`I = X_cur / gain_cur` (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a
95	nominal bias. Gains come from `measurement_config`. Raises if not exactly one
96	current channel is resolvable. `channels` restricts the voltage channels
97	returned. Returned R is **signed** (X/I): take `np.abs` for Rxx, keep the sign
98	for Rxy/Hall.
99	
100	### `ResistanceGrids` (dataclass)
101	`current` (I grid, A), `current_channel` (cid), `R` (dict: voltage cid →
102	signed R grid, Ω).
103	
104	---
105	
106	## Shubnikov–de Haas
107	
108	### `field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` → `np.ndarray`
109	`N` field points from `B_start` to `B_end`, **uniform in 1/B** (SdH
110	oscillations are periodic in 1/B). Both endpoints must be `> 0`. Argument order
111	sets sweep direction. Sweeping these setpoints hands `sdh_fft` an already-even
112	1/B record (no resample needed).
113	
114	### `sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=None, nfft=512, bg_degree=5, window='hann', log=True, floor=1.0, uniform_rtol=0.1)` → `(freqs, spec)`
115	Per-column SdH FFT in 1/B.
116	
117	- **Input `R_grid` is `(n_B, n_fast)`** — rows are field (the `FanGrids` row
118	  axis), columns are the fast axis. **2-D is required**; a single trace must be
119	  passed as `R[:, None]` (and the output column squeezed back). Raises if
120	  `R_grid.shape[0] != len(B)`.
121	- `B` is the per-row field `(n_B,)`, arbitrarily spaced.
122	- Per column: select `b_range`, optionally `log10(max(R, floor))`, subtract a
123	  degree-`bg_degree` polynomial background **in B-space** (`None` skips — the
124	  magnetoresistance background is smooth in B, not 1/B, so it is removed before
125	  the 1/B step), then FFT in 1/B. The 1/B resample is conditional: data already
126	  uniform in 1/B (decided from the spacing distribution within `uniform_rtol`)
127	  is FFT'd directly, zero-padded to `nfft`; uniform-in-B data is interpolated
128	  onto a regular `nfft`-point 1/B grid.
129	- **Returns `(freqs, spec)`**: `freqs` in Tesla `(n_freq,)`, `spec` the FFT
130	  magnitude **`(n_fast, n_freq)`** (note the transpose vs the input).
131	
132	### `sdh_onset(R, B, *, b_hi=None, b_lo=0.3, r_full_scale=None, headroom=0.95, bg_degree=5, f_min=3.0, snr_threshold=5.0, n_periods=3.0, min_periods=2.0, step_frac=0.25, gap_widths=0.5, min_pts=8, max_tones=8, tone_floor_mult=4.0, marginal_mult=2.0)` → `SdhOnset`
133	Per-tone low-B onsets of the SdH oscillations in a single trace.
134	**`R` is a single 1-D longitudinal-resistance trace `(n_B,)`** (contrast
135	`sdh_fft`'s 2-D grid); `B` is the matching field `(n_B,)`. Removes a B-space
136	polynomial background, identifies every SdH tone via nested high-B FFT scans,
137	then walks each tone's Gaussian matched filter (FWHM = `n_periods` periods of
138	that tone) from high B down to where its amplitude sinks into the record's
139	white-noise floor — a statistical (≈`snr_threshold`·σ) onset, which can
140	legitimately sit below a by-eye read. `onset_b` is the minimum onset over
141	robust tones — the `landau-fan` step-1 `B_lo`, correct even when a light tone
142	outlives the dominant one. Pass `r_full_scale` (sensitivity / I_bias, Ω) to
143	enable soft-clip detection: samples ≥ `headroom`× full scale truncate the
144	analysis window (reported via `clip_high_b`) with a warning.
145	**Failure is never a nan** — raises `SdhOnsetError` (a `ValueError`: record
146	too short, no tones above the spectral floor, or no tone trackable) with
147	specifics; partial failures warn and land in `.untracked`.
148	
149	### `SdhOnset` (dataclass)
150	`onset_b` (min onset over robust tones, Tesla — the record's low edge, flagged,
151	when the carrying tone is *censored*, i.e. still above threshold at the last
152	window), `onset_freq` (tone carrying it), `clip_high_b` / `b_lo_record` (the
153	analyzed window's edges), `noise_sigma`, `tones` (list of `SdhTone`, contrast
154	descending), `untracked` (`(freq, reason)` pairs). Convenience properties map
155	to the dominant tone: `consensus_freq`, `b_centers`, `snr` (the old
156	`peak_freq` field is gone). `summary()` renders the whole read — headline,
157	per-tone table with flags, untracked reasons — for a notebook cell.
158	
159	### `SdhTone` (dataclass)
160	One tone's track: `freq`, `contrast`, `onset_b`, flags `censored` /
161	`revived` (above-threshold windows exist below the gap-walk stop) /
162	`marginal` (peak SNR < `marginal_mult`×threshold; excluded from the headline) /
163	`near_residual` (filter passband overlaps the detrend-residual band; excluded
164	from the headline unless a tracked harmonic corroborates it), `n_periods` /
165	`win_invB` (actual filter geometry), `harmonic_of` (freq of the stronger tone
166	this sits at ~k× of, else `None`), curves `b_centers` / `snr` / `amp`, and
167	`delta_f(b_max)` — the per-tone FFT resolution `1/(1/onset_b − 1/b_max)`.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Gate calibration
172	
173	> **Units — SI.** `GateCalibration` and `luttinger_frequency` work entirely in
174	> SI: density **n in m⁻²**, displacement field **D in V/m**, frequency in
175	> Tesla. (For the conventional ×10¹² cm⁻² display unit, scale n by `1e-16`.)
176	> The separate `sharpelab_nb.gates` conversion helpers (`calc_nD`,
177	> `calc_gate_voltages`, …) use **n in 10¹² cm⁻²** — do not feed an SI density
178	> from here into those, or vice versa.
179	
180	### `GateCalibration` (frozen dataclass)
181	`GateCalibration(c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0)` — areal capacitances
182	(F/m²), `n_offset` (m⁻²), `D_offset` (V/m). Construct once per session, then:
183	
184	```
185	n = (c_tg·V_tg + c_bg·V_bg) / e   + n_offset      [m⁻²]
186	D = (c_tg·V_tg − c_bg·V_bg) / (2·ε₀) + D_offset   [V/m]
187	```
188	
189	- `density(V_tg, V_bg)` → n `(m⁻²)`.
190	- `displacement_field(V_tg, V_bg)` → D `(V/m)`.
191	- `n_D(V_tg, V_bg)` → `(n, D)`.
192	- `from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2=0.0, *, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0, kappa_hBN=3.0, kappa_SiO2=3.9)` — build from gate-stack geometry (metres) instead of areal capacitances; `t_bgSiO2=0` for a metal/graphite back gate.
193	
194	All accept scalars or arrays. Physical constants come from `scipy.constants`.
195	
196	### `luttinger_frequency(n)` → `np.ndarray`
197	Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla, for a
198	single Fermi surface carrying the full density. **`n` is in SI m⁻²** — feed
199	`GateCalibration.density` output directly. The 4 is the spin×valley Landau
200	degeneracy; returns the `|n|` form (positive for either carrier sign).

# `hera.analysis` API Reference

Analysis primitives for `sweep` runs: open + summarize a run, resolve lock-in
channels and gains, re-form 2D fans into grids, compute gain-applied
resistances, and the Shubnikov–de Haas / gate-calibration math.

Source: `src/hera/analysis.py`. Depends only on `numpy` + `scipy`.

A *run* is a directory written by `sweep`: `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless, one row
per setpoint) + `metadata.json` (column names, sweep config, comments).

---

## Loading runs

### `open_run(path)` → `Run`
Open a run directory (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Loads `metadata.json` and
`data.tsv(.gz)` into an `(rows, ncols)` float array; raises if the directory,
`metadata.json`, the `columns` entry, or the TSV is missing, or if the column
count disagrees with `metadata['columns']`.

### `Run` (dataclass)
`Run(path, meta, cols, data)`.

| member | description |
|---|---|
| `col(name)` | column `name` as a 1-D array; raises `KeyError` if absent, `ValueError` if the name is duplicated (use `col_at`) |
| `col_at(idx)` | column by index |
| `col_indices(name)` | all indices with column name `name` |
| `metadata` | alias for `meta` (the parsed `metadata.json` dict) |
| `recipe` | first metadata comment (conventional recipe slug), or `None` |
| `tags` | comments after the first |
| `swept_axis` | `metadata['param']` (1D sweeps) |
| `setpoints` | `metadata['setpoints']` as a list, or `None` |
| `interrupted` | `metadata['interrupted']` |
| `kind` | `metadata['type']` (`'0D'`/`'1D'`/`'2D'`) |
| `rows` | row count |

Duplicate column names occur (planned setpoint + readback share a name; some
older data has two `T` columns). `col(name)` raises on duplicates — resolve
with `col_indices` + `col_at`.

### `summarize_run(run)` → `str`
Multi-line human summary: recipe, type, sweep range + monotonicity, row
completeness vs planned setpoints, and mean/range T if a `T` column is present.
Lines with no data are omitted.

---

## Lock-in channel / gain model

Shared with `hera.watch`. The physical value of a lock-in `*_X` column is
`X / gain`, with the gain read from `measurement_config` — never hardcode it.

### `resolve_channels(meta, include=None)` → `list[Channel]`
Resolve every `_X` (in-phase) column into a `Channel`. Gains and role labels
come from `meta['measurement_config']`, matched `srN_X` ↔ `srN_gain` by the
channel's trailing integer (so both `sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain` and `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`
resolve); missing/zero gain defaults to `1.0`. `include` restricts to given
channel ids or column names. A channel `is_current` (reported as amps, not
converted to resistance) when its gain is negative, `|gain| ≥ 1e4`, or its
label mentions "current".

### `Channel` (dataclass)
`col` (e.g. `'sr0_X'`), `idx` (column index), `cid` (id without `_X`), `n`
(trailing-integer index), `gain`, `label` (mc role string), `is_current`.

### `current_channel(channels)` → `Channel | None`
The single transimpedance current channel, or `None` if not exactly one. This
is the denominator of four-probe resistance R = V / I.

---

## Fan re-forming and resistances

### `fan_grids(run, columns=None)` → `FanGrids`
Re-form a 2D fan (a flat-row `megasweep`/`multimegasweep`) into per-column
grids, keeping only complete slow rows. `run` is a directory, path, or loaded
`Run`. `nfast` (points per slow row) comes from `metadata['fast_setpoints']`
— never hardcoded; trailing partial rows of an in-progress sweep are dropped
(`nrows = total // nfast`). `columns` restricts which columns are retained.

### `FanGrids` (dataclass)
`nrows`, `nfast`, `cols`, `data` (truncated to whole rows), `meta`,
`slow_param`.
- `grid(name)` → `(nrows, nfast)` array (duplicate names resolve to the first
  occurrence, i.e. the planned setpoint).
- `slow` → slow-axis value per row, `(nrows,)`.
- `metadata` → alias for `meta`.

### `resistance_grids(fan, channels=None)` → `ResistanceGrids`
Per-channel four-probe resistance grids `R = (V / gain_V) / I` from a
`FanGrids`, where `I` is the **measured** drain current
`I = X_cur / gain_cur` (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a
nominal bias. Gains come from `measurement_config`. Raises if not exactly one
current channel is resolvable. `channels` restricts the voltage channels
returned. Returned R is **signed** (X/I): take `np.abs` for Rxx, keep the sign
for Rxy/Hall.

### `ResistanceGrids` (dataclass)
`current` (I grid, A), `current_channel` (cid), `R` (dict: voltage cid →
signed R grid, Ω).

---

## Shubnikov–de Haas

### `field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` → `np.ndarray`
`N` field points from `B_start` to `B_end`, **uniform in 1/B** (SdH
oscillations are periodic in 1/B). Both endpoints must be `> 0`. Argument order
sets sweep direction. Sweeping these setpoints hands `sdh_fft` an already-even
1/B record (no resample needed).

### `sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=None, nfft=512, bg_degree=5, window='hann', log=True, floor=1.0, uniform_rtol=0.1)` → `(freqs, spec)`
Per-column SdH FFT in 1/B.

- **Input `R_grid` is `(n_B, n_fast)`** — rows are field (the `FanGrids` row
  axis), columns are the fast axis. **2-D is required**; a single trace must be
  passed as `R[:, None]` (and the output column squeezed back). Raises if
  `R_grid.shape[0] != len(B)`.
- `B` is the per-row field `(n_B,)`, arbitrarily spaced.
- Per column: select `b_range`, optionally `log10(max(R, floor))`, subtract a
  degree-`bg_degree` polynomial background **in B-space** (`None` skips — the
  magnetoresistance background is smooth in B, not 1/B, so it is removed before
  the 1/B step), then FFT in 1/B. The 1/B resample is conditional: data already
  uniform in 1/B (decided from the spacing distribution within `uniform_rtol`)
  is FFT'd directly, zero-padded to `nfft`; uniform-in-B data is interpolated
  onto a regular `nfft`-point 1/B grid.
- **Returns `(freqs, spec)`**: `freqs` in Tesla `(n_freq,)`, `spec` the FFT
  magnitude **`(n_fast, n_freq)`** (note the transpose vs the input).

### `sdh_onset(R, B, *, b_hi=None, b_lo=0.3, r_full_scale=None, headroom=0.95, bg_degree=5, f_min=3.0, snr_threshold=5.0, n_periods=3.0, min_periods=2.0, step_frac=0.25, gap_widths=0.5, min_pts=8, max_tones=8, tone_floor_mult=4.0, marginal_mult=2.0)` → `SdhOnset`
Per-tone low-B onsets of the SdH oscillations in a single trace.
**`R` is a single 1-D longitudinal-resistance trace `(n_B,)`** (contrast
`sdh_fft`'s 2-D grid); `B` is the matching field `(n_B,)`. Removes a B-space
polynomial background, identifies every SdH tone via nested high-B FFT scans,
then walks each tone's Gaussian matched filter (FWHM = `n_periods` periods of
that tone) from high B down to where its amplitude sinks into the record's
white-noise floor — a statistical (≈`snr_threshold`·σ) onset, which can
legitimately sit below a by-eye read. `onset_b` is the minimum onset over
robust tones — the `landau-fan` step-1 `B_lo`, correct even when a light tone
outlives the dominant one. Pass `r_full_scale` (sensitivity / I_bias, Ω) to
enable soft-clip detection: samples ≥ `headroom`× full scale truncate the
analysis window (reported via `clip_high_b`) with a warning.
**Failure is never a nan** — raises `SdhOnsetError` (a `ValueError`: record
too short, no tones above the spectral floor, or no tone trackable) with
specifics; partial failures warn and land in `.untracked`.

### `SdhOnset` (dataclass)
`onset_b` (min onset over robust tones, Tesla — the record's low edge, flagged,
when the carrying tone is *censored*, i.e. still above threshold at the last
window), `onset_freq` (tone carrying it), `clip_high_b` / `b_lo_record` (the
analyzed window's edges), `noise_sigma`, `tones` (list of `SdhTone`, contrast
descending), `untracked` (`(freq, reason)` pairs). Convenience properties map
to the dominant tone: `consensus_freq`, `b_centers`, `snr` (the old
`peak_freq` field is gone). `summary()` renders the whole read — headline,
per-tone table with flags, untracked reasons — for a notebook cell.

### `SdhTone` (dataclass)
One tone's track: `freq`, `contrast`, `onset_b`, flags `censored` /
`revived` (above-threshold windows exist below the gap-walk stop) /
`marginal` (peak SNR < `marginal_mult`×threshold; excluded from the headline) /
`near_residual` (filter passband overlaps the detrend-residual band; excluded
from the headline unless a tracked harmonic corroborates it), `n_periods` /
`win_invB` (actual filter geometry), `harmonic_of` (freq of the stronger tone
this sits at ~k× of, else `None`), curves `b_centers` / `snr` / `amp`, and
`delta_f(b_max)` — the per-tone FFT resolution `1/(1/onset_b − 1/b_max)`.

---

## Gate calibration

> **Units — SI.** `GateCalibration` and `luttinger_frequency` work entirely in
> SI: density **n in m⁻²**, displacement field **D in V/m**, frequency in
> Tesla. (For the conventional ×10¹² cm⁻² display unit, scale n by `1e-16`.)
> The separate `sharpelab_nb.gates` conversion helpers (`calc_nD`,
> `calc_gate_voltages`, …) use **n in 10¹² cm⁻²** — do not feed an SI density
> from here into those, or vice versa.

### `GateCalibration` (frozen dataclass)
`GateCalibration(c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0)` — areal capacitances
(F/m²), `n_offset` (m⁻²), `D_offset` (V/m). Construct once per session, then:

```
n = (c_tg·V_tg + c_bg·V_bg) / e   + n_offset      [m⁻²]
D = (c_tg·V_tg − c_bg·V_bg) / (2·ε₀) + D_offset   [V/m]
```

- `density(V_tg, V_bg)` → n `(m⁻²)`.
- `displacement_field(V_tg, V_bg)` → D `(V/m)`.
- `n_D(V_tg, V_bg)` → `(n, D)`.
- `from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2=0.0, *, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0, kappa_hBN=3.0, kappa_SiO2=3.9)` — build from gate-stack geometry (metres) instead of areal capacitances; `t_bgSiO2=0` for a metal/graphite back gate.

All accept scalars or arrays. Physical constants come from `scipy.constants`.

### `luttinger_frequency(n)` → `np.ndarray`
Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla, for a
single Fermi surface carrying the full density. **`n` is in SI m⁻²** — feed
`GateCalibration.density` output directly. The 4 is the spin×valley Landau
degeneracy; returns the `|n|` form (positive for either carrier sign).

1	# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference
2	
3	The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
4	`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
5	each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.
6	
7	Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
8	`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
9	`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Station
14	
15	### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
16	A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
17	is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
18	gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
19	`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
20	into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.
21	
22	### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
23	Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
24	are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
25	executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
26	batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
27	SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
28	default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.
29	
30	### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
31	Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
32	**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
33	so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
34	follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.
35	
36	### `add_comment(comment)`
37	Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
38	every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
39	metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
40	intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.
41	
42	### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
43	Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
44	ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).
45	
46	### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
47	Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
48	is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
49	name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
50	declares):
51	
52	| context key | available in | value |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
55	| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
56	| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |
57	
58	A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
59	`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
60	`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
61	be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
62	is seen through the partial, so injection still works).
63	
64	### Other methods
65	- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
66	- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
67	  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
68	- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
69	- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
70	- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Sweeps
75	
76	Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
77	**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
78	`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
79	gain-divided.
80	
81	| method | signature | row layout |
82	|---|---|---|
83	| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
84	| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
85	| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
86	| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
